title: Inside the Abandoned Riverside Asylum (Before It's Demolished)
creator: Concrete & Dust
description:
We got permission from the site owner to film inside before demolition starts next month. Please don't try to visit, it's fenced, patrolled, and genuinely dangerous.

Today's video is supported by the Harbor Lights Shelter Network, which runs emergency beds and winter outreach across the region. Give a night of shelter: harborlights.org/give

Camera: DJI Osmo Pocket 3
Members get the uncut walkthrough: join button above

#urbex #abandoned

sentences.t: Alright, we're in, and before anything else, yes, we have permission to be here, the owner let us in for one afternoon.
This place is coming down next month, so this is probably the last time anyone films inside.
It opened in the late 1800s as a hospital, and it's been empty since, I think, 1994.
Watch your step here, the floor's gone soft by the door.
Okay, this is the main corridor, and it just keeps going, look at that.
You can still see the old paint, that pale green they used everywhere because it was supposed to be calming.
It's not calming, for the record.
Jess, can you shine your light up there?
See the hooks on the ceiling, those held the old gas lamps before they wired the place.
And there's a room up here on the left that the owner told us about specifically.
This was the day room, where patients would sit when they weren't on the wards.
There's still a piano, I can't believe nobody took it.
Let me see if it plays.
Oh, nope, that is the saddest sound I've ever heard.
The windows in here are huge, which, apparently, was the whole idea, light and air were supposed to be the treatment.
Okay, we're heading down to the basement, which is where the boiler rooms are.
It's really wet down here, there's maybe two inches of water on the floor.
And that's the original boiler, look at the size of it, it's like a train engine lying on its side.
This thing heated the entire building, every ward, every corridor, through all those pipes running along the ceiling.
Jess just found a stack of old ledgers in the corner.
These are coal deliveries, dates and tons, all handwritten, 1920s by the look of it.
We're going to leave them for the local archive, the owner said they want anything with writing on it.
Alright, last stop is the roof, and then we're out of here before the light goes.
Wow, okay, you can see the whole river from up here.
They built it on the hill on purpose, they really believed the view would help people get better.
And honestly, standing up here, I kind of get it.
So that's it, that's the last look inside this place before it's gone.
Thanks for walking through it with us, and remember, don't go into buildings like this without permission, it's not worth it.
Before you go, I want to take a second for the organization that supported today's video.
This video is brought to you by the Harbor Lights Shelter Network.
A lot of empty buildings like this one end up being the only shelter some people have, especially in winter.
Harbor Lights runs emergency beds and night outreach vans across the region, so people have somewhere safe to go instead.
Thirty dollars covers one night in a warm bed, with a hot meal and someone to talk to about next steps.
You can give a night of shelter at harborlights.org slash give, and that link is right at the top of the description.
Thanks so much to Harbor Lights for sponsoring this one, and to everyone who chips in.
We'll see you in the next building.
